title: Apple starts giving Siri AI access to third-party apps
slides: Can Siri finally call the shots on your apps?
Apple opened Siri to third-party app controls
But only a handful of apps work at launch
Your daily routines may now run without touching the screen
Start mapping which app handoffs matter most
thread_text:
1. The real Siri test

For the first time, Apple lets Siri control third-party apps, like sending a message or booking a ride, without opening them. But only a few apps work at launch.

2. Apple's quiet shift

By opening Siri to outside developers, Apple admits its assistant can't do everything alone. The move puts Siri in direct competition with Google Assistant and Alexa.

3. Barely a handful

Only a tiny list of apps supports the new controls now. That means most of your daily apps still need a tap, so the dream of full hands-free is far off.

4. Routines without touch

Early testers say simple routines like texting a contact or ordering food now work hands-free. But if an app isn't on the list, the chain breaks and you're back to tapping.

5. Map your handoffs

List the five app actions you do most each day. Check if each one works with Siri today, and if not, decide whether to wait or change your routine now.
